purpose: Behavior fixtures for Python Agent engineering discipline derived from the design-first, explicit-state, strict-tool-contract, bounded-loop, resilience, and self-validation workflow.

scenarios.request: The model calls search_docs with queryText but the registered tool requires query.
must_do: validate or repair structured arguments before invocation
separate model-output error from tool-runtime error
must_not: send an invalid call and treat the tool failure as normal reasoning

scenarios.request: A multi-turn agent forgets which task IDs were already completed after a restart.
must_not: rely on conversation text as the only state store
hide durable state in a module global

scenarios.request: A ReAct agent keeps retrying the same tool after the same error.
A write tool times out after the remote service may already have committed the change.
must_do: use idempotency or reconciliation before replay
preserve evidence of attempted side effect
must_not: assume timeout means no mutation occurred

scenarios.request: Add a new LangGraph node that mutates shared workflow state.
must_do: design the state transition before coding
must_not: treat graph topology alone as proof of correctness

scenarios.request: A planner hands execution to two workers that may update the same task record.
must_not: let both workers become independent authorities

scenarios.request: The model provider returns rate limits and intermittent malformed responses.
must_do: expose retry exhaustion to agent state

scenarios.request: The user says directly implement the Python agent fix now.
must_do: establish a compact design contract first
proceed in the same authorized execution cycle
